title: ifo Business Climate Index
text: start creating theme somewhat similar style ifo website. information create custom themes, see ggplot2 documentation see examples themes ggthemes package.
code: library(ggplot2)  theme_ifo <- function(...) {   theme_minimal(...) +     theme(       legend.title = element_blank(),       legend.position = "top",       plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),       plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 8, margin = margin(10, 0, 0, 0)),       panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.2),       panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),       panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),       axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),       axis.title = element_blank(),       plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)     ) }

title: ifo Business Climate Index
code: library(ifo)  climate <- ifo_business()  climate |>   subset(series == "index") |>   ggplot(aes(x = yearmonth, y = value, color = indicator)) +   geom_line() +   labs(     title = "ifo Business Climate Germany",     subtitle = "Seasonally adjusted",     caption = sprintf("Source: ifo Business Survey, %s.", format(max(climate$yearmonth), "%B %Y"))   ) +   scale_color_manual(     values = c(climate = "darkred", situation = "darkgrey", expectation = "darkblue"),     labels = c(       climate = "ifo Business Climate",       situation = "Assessment of Business Situation",       expectation = "Business Expectation"     )   ) +   theme_ifo()

title: ifo Business Climate Index
code: sectors <- ifo_business("sectors") |>   subset(     series == "balance" &       sector %in% c("manufacturing", "services", "trade", "construction") &       yearmonth >= "2020-01-01"   ) |>   transform(     sector = factor(sector, levels = c("manufacturing", "services", "trade", "construction"))   )  ggplot(sectors, aes(x = yearmonth, y = value, color = indicator)) +   geom_line() +   facet_wrap(     ~sector,     labeller = labeller(       sector = c(         manufacturing = "Manufacturing",         services = "Service Sector",         trade = "Trade",         construction = "Construction"       )     )   ) +   labs(     title = "ifo Business Climate by Sector",     subtitle = "Balances, seasonally adjusted",     caption = sprintf("Source: ifo Business Survey, %s.", format(max(sectors$yearmonth), "%B %Y"))   ) +   scale_color_manual(     values = c(climate = "darkred", situation = "darkgrey", expectation = "darkblue"),     labels = c(       climate = "ifo Business Climate",       situation = "Assessment of Business Situation",       expectation = "Business Expectation"     )   ) +   theme_ifo()

title: ifo Business Climate Index
code: climate |>   subset(select = c(yearmonth, uncertainty)) |>   na.omit() |>   ggplot(aes(x = yearmonth, y = uncertainty)) +   geom_line() +   labs(     title = "ifo Business Uncertainty Germany",     subtitle = "Original values",     caption = sprintf("Source: ifo Business Survey, %s.", format(max(climate$yearmonth), "%B %Y"))   ) +   theme_ifo()

title: Return ifo business climate vintage data — ifo_vintage
text: vintage time series published given month. vintage runs start series release month, later vintages contain months may revise earlier values, example seasonal adjustment. output contains one observation per row value. columns describe observation: yearmonth: observed month. vintage: first day month series published. indicator: climate, situation, expectation. series: index balance. type = "germany" type = "industry" return index 2015 = 100. sectors return balances. type = "industry" corresponds "Industry Trade" source. ifo updates vintage workbooks less often monthly releases, latest vintage can lag current ifo_business() release several months.
